pathwayLabel: Additional justice-court or municipal-court misdemeanor relief
packetFamilyLabel: Discretionary Expungement of Additional Justice Court or Municipal Court Misdemeanors

legalSectionsBoundBy.scope: The exact existing family documents, both enumerated lower-court runtime routes, and canonical and boundary artifact hashes recorded below; no runtime, technical, payment, sponsorship, or production authority.

generatedBy: route-productization worker from existing owner-approved records; no new legal or source authority
specificationNote: This one family specification enumerates exactly the parallel justice-court and municipal-court runtime routes. It binds the existing five-component census-v1 family and its adopted canonical and boundary hashes. The venue branch selects the court and section; it does not create a third route, authorize a sibling Mississippi route, or grant fulfillment or commercial authority.

statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: The parallel provisions give the justice court or municipal court discretionary power to expunge any or all misdemeanor convictions in that same court after an open-court showing of rehabilitation, good conduct for two years since the last conviction in any court, and the best interest of society. The order does not reach confidential law-enforcement records and has no effect on the Title 63 driving record.
doNotImport: Do not merge convictions from different courts into one petition; each court reaches only its own misdemeanor convictions.
Do not apply the fee in § 99-19-72, which by its terms applies to petitions under § 99-19-71, to either route.
Do not promise that confidential law-enforcement records or the Title 63 driving record will be cleared.
Do not write the participant's open-court rehabilitation, good-conduct, or best-interest showing.
Do not extend this family to another Mississippi pathway.

finalVerificationRequirements: The server-owned route is exactly the justice-court or municipal-court pathway; a client-supplied family or section never chooses it.
Copy the court, place, cause number, petitioner caption name, and every conviction from certified judgments from that one court.
Confirm the date of the last conviction in any court from a criminal-history record and verify that the two-year period has elapsed.
Confirm the correct prosecuting authority and current service address with the clerk of the petitioned court.
The participant signs and dates the petition and certificate; the prosecutor and judge complete their own protected fields.
The participant makes the rehabilitation, good-conduct, and best-interest showing in open court; the packet writes none of it.

participantChecklist.text: Confirm that every conviction listed belongs to the one justice or municipal court named in the caption.
Confirm from criminal history that two years have passed since the last conviction in any court.
Ask the clerk about any local form, fee or waiver, copy count, filing method, hearing setting, and proposed-order practice.
Confirm and serve the correct prosecuting authority for the selected lower-court branch.
